feat(output): carry a schema version in every json payload (S51, ADR-070)

A reader parsing --json had no way to notice that a field had moved: the
parse succeeds, the lookup returns undefined, and the answer is quietly
wrong. schemaVersion now travels inside the document, because a version in
a comment is the artefact that goes stale without failing anything.

The same document is one line instead of four columns of whitespace. The
reader of --json is a program and it pays for every byte; --pretty asks for
the other form, and a terminal gets it without being asked because there
the reader is a person.

The shape is decided once in dispatch rather than at twenty-five call
sites, so a new command cannot have a private idea of what --json means.
Writing the contract test found eight commands that already did: they
hand-rolled emit(JSON.stringify(..., null, 2)) instead of the shared
helper, so --json meant something different depending on which command you
asked. It also found that fail() wrote only to stderr, which meant a
command that failed under --json handed a scripted caller an empty document
and an exit code and nothing else; a failure is a result and now answers in
the shape it was asked in.
f2p: a reader that asks for pretty gets pretty
every command that emits json emits one compact document with a version
the version is the payload's, not the documentation's
